actor_type.description: A patient of the trust — carries demographics (deprivation decile, ethnicity), clinical attributes (primary condition, frailty, comorbidities) and pathway flags that steer them through the care pathways.

status.description: The booking holds a live reserved opening, pending attend.
The subject attended the confirmed opening (terminal).
The subject drew a no-show at the confirmed opening; the slot is wasted, not returned (terminal).
The booking was released before attend by an explicit cancel (terminal).
The booking was released before attend because the subject's patience expired (terminal).
The booking's opening was cut by a diary cancel_rebook resolution and rebooked to a successor (terminal).
The booking's opening was cut by a diary forfeit resolution with no successor (terminal).

booking_discipline.description: Assigns the earliest eligible opening — an eligible free-list entry when one exists, else the diary's cursor.

diary_type.description: A per-specialty outpatient clinic appointment book. The wait for a routine slot emerges from how fast referrals arrive against a fixed supply of openings.
A per-specialty two-week-wait cancer clinic book for urgent suspected-cancer referrals; the 2WW wait is the booking lead-time.
A per-specialty elective operating-list book; the wait for surgery emerges from scarce theatre-list openings.

entity_type.description: An inpatient ward with a bed count and a ward type (general, assessment, ICU/HDU, step-down) that stratifies safety-incident risk.
An operating theatre, with a specialty and a number of operating sessions per day.
A diagnostic test type (X-ray, CT, MRI, bloods, ECG, ultrasound and others) with a typical turnaround and cost.
A surgical procedure in the catalogue, coded by OPCS-4 with an HRG case-mix bucket, national tariff and complexity band.
A medication in the formulary, grouped by drug class and specialty.

current_state.description: Newly arrived patient awaiting routing to a care pathway.
Routed to the emergency (A&E) pathway.
Routed to the elective outpatient pathway.
Routed to the suspected-cancer pathway.
Routed to the elective surgical pathway.
Arrived in A&E, waiting for an emergency doctor to triage them.
Triaged in A&E; awaiting clinical assessment.
Assessed by the emergency team; awaiting a diagnosis and any diagnostic tests.
Diagnosed in A&E; a decision is made to discharge home or admit.
Discharged home from A&E.
Admitted from A&E to an inpatient bed.
Admitted patient being booked in and matched to a specialty consultant, waiting if the specialty is full.
Allocated to an inpatient ward.
Receiving specialty inpatient care; length of stay varies by condition, with a daily risk of a safety incident and a frailty-driven risk of death.
Escalated to intensive care for the sickest patients.
Declared medically fit for discharge; either discharged or held for a delayed transfer of care.
Medically fit but waiting for community or social care to be arranged (a delayed transfer of care); the wait lengthens with deprivation.
Discharged from the inpatient ward.
Died in hospital during the inpatient stay.
Referred by a GP to an outpatient clinic.
On the waiting list for a clinic appointment, with a daily risk of deteriorating while waiting.
Attended the outpatient appointment.
Did not attend (DNA) the booked appointment, wasting the slot.
Outpatient episode complete after attending.
Outpatient episode closed after a missed appointment.
Diagnostic test being scheduled.
Test scheduling deferred into a backlog before being ordered.
Test ordered; awaiting the test to be performed (turnaround varies by modality).
Test performed; awaiting the report.
Test reported; result being communicated.
Diagnostic result communicated to the requesting team.
Urgent cancer referral being processed.
Cancer referral held in a backlog before proceeding.
Two-week-wait referral made; awaiting a first specialist appointment.
Waiting for the first two-week-wait clinic appointment.
Seen by the specialist for the first time.
Cancer diagnosis confirmed.
Treatment decision made (decision-to-treat).
Cancer treatment started.
Pre-operative assessment; the procedure is planned and the patient is listed for surgery.
On the elective waiting list for an operating-list slot.
Day of surgery; a specialty surgeon is taken for the operation.
Operation performed in theatre.
Recovering after the operation.
Post-operative review; the surgical episode is complete.
Recently discharged and recovering at home; an FFT invitation is sent.
Follow-up check; the patient either recovers or is readmitted, with risk rising by comorbidity burden.
Being readmitted as an emergency, starting a new inpatient spell.
Recovered after discharge; the episode is closed.
Readmission recorded; a fresh inpatient spell is underway.
Invited to complete the Friends and Family Test after discharge.
Responded to the survey with a satisfaction score.
Did not respond to the survey.

journey_type.description: Front-door triage that routes each new arrival to the right pathway — emergency, elective outpatient, cancer or surgical — by pathway type.
An A&E (emergency department) attendance: arrival, triage, assessment, diagnosis, then either discharge home or admission to a ward.
An inpatient hospital stay from admission through ward care (and possible ICU escalation or death) to medically-fit, any delayed transfer of care, and discharge.
An elective outpatient referral: wait for a clinic appointment, then either attend or do-not-attend (DNA).
A diagnostic test order running alongside an A&E or outpatient episode: scheduling, the test being performed, reported, and the result communicated.
A suspected-cancer pathway on the two-week-wait standard: referral, first appointment, diagnosis, treatment decision and start of treatment, tracked against the 62-day target.
An elective surgical pathway: pre-operative assessment, wait for an operating-list slot, the operation itself, and recovery to post-op review.
Follow-up after an inpatient discharge: a check at home that either resolves to recovery or to an emergency readmission.
The Friends and Family Test — every discharged patient is invited to rate their care; they either respond with a score or do not respond.

discipline.description: Waiters promoted by highest declared priority, ties by earliest enqueue.
A newly-arriving higher-priority actor displaces a lower-priority holder; 1-server queues only.

on_full.description: The seize waits in the queue for a slot to free.
The seize is rejected immediately and routed to its on_rejected handler.
The seize resamples a delay and is retried.
The seize is routed to its on_reroute handler.

resource_type.description: A senior doctor with finite capacity, deliberately split by pathway: ward admissions gate themselves below full capacity to hold slots back for clinic and theatre work, so an inpatient side that plateaus short of the declared capacity is the specialty running full. Consultants of the same specialty share one priority queue, and a saturated specialty queues its patients by clinical priority.

scenario_description: An acute NHS hospital trust: emergency and elective patients flow from a single arrivals stream through A&E, inpatient wards, outpatient clinics, diagnostics, cancer and surgical pathways, then post-discharge follow-up — competing for consultants, beds, theatres and clinic slots under seasonal demand pressure.
